note: Adapted from Emerson 1956; the original is in English. In Table 1 the paratype values for head thickness and hind tibia length are left blank with a dash (—) (not given in the original) and are reproduced as such; the description of this species rests mainly on the differential comparison with A. desneuxi, and no separate morphological illustrations are given.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier very close to A. desneuxi. It differs in the outline of the vertex: in the present species the head rises rather evenly between the frons and the vertex, whereas in the paratype soldiers of A. desneuxi (2 from the Inkisi type colony, Congo, and 1 from Leopoldville) the frons and vertex meet at an angle and the vertex outline is flatter. The author notes that this difference in head shape has only provisional taxonomic value and may still fall within the normal variation of A. desneuxi. The postmentum, pronotum and fore coxae all resemble those of A. desneuxi.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head rising rather evenly between the frons and the vertex; the remaining morphology, the figures and the measurements are close to the description of A. desneuxi (Emerson, 1953, pp. 108-113). Some setae of the dried holotype may have been worn off. The postmentum, pronotum and fore coxae are very similar to those of A. desneuxi. Measurements (mm, holotype Lunda / paratype Dundo): head length including mandibles 4.63 / 3.80; head length to the lateral base of the mandibles 3.21 / 2.70; head width 2.51 / 2.10; head thickness 1.77 / —; postmentum length 2.04 / 1.60; postmentum maximum width 0.73 / 0.59; postmentum minimum width 0.67 / 0.44; left mandible length 1.81 / 1.50; pronotum length 0.96 / 0.90; pronotum width 1.94 / 2.00; hind tibia length 1.96 / —.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The specimens are in poor condition; on the characters of the legs they approach A. lamani; the comparison of the individual workers is given in the phylogenetic discussion at the end of the paper.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The single dried holotype soldier was obtained by W. V. Harris, together with workers, from a nest collected by A. W. Exell in Lunda, Angola (near Vila Henrique de Carvalho), in April 1937 (month 4), in sandy soil; the holotype and the nest are both deposited in the Natural History Museum, London. The paratype colony comes from Dundo, Angola, collected by A. de Barros Machodo and sent by H. Weidner. Nests believed to belong to this species are recorded from Kondue (Sankuru District), Mayidi (near Kisantu) and the Plateau de Kamina (Lualaba) in the Belgian Congo, and from the Haut Zambèze in Angola. Weidner (1955, p. 204) had described the Dundo nest as the new species A. machodoensis, and later assigned its specimens to the present species as a paratype colony.
